question.text: A block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> slides on an inclined plane which makes an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the block and the surface is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. The force along the plane that needs to be applied to the block so that it moves up without any acceleration is ( take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> )

solution.text:
For acceleration to be zero, the net force should be zero.

F=mgsinθ+μmgcosθ⇒F=2×10×12+32×2×10×32⇒F=25 N
